request.spec:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added an Activity panel to the sheet screen. Pressing Show lists one line per user and event, `<user> <EVENT> <count>`, sorted by user and then by event. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the activity test and the three existing scenarios).

How it works:
- **Server:** a new `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/activity` endpoint (`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/activity.GET.yml`) is backed by `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/RespondWithActivity.java`. It reads only this sheet's lines from the audit file through the existing audit service and counts each event by the user in `by=`. It writes nothing to the audit file and doesn't change any stored data, so there's no schema change.
- **Front end:** the panel is in `src/main/frontend/features/activity/activity.slot.tsx`, using the `activity-show` and `activity-line` test ids. It sits just after the Audit panel and works the same way: the old lines clear on each press, so two presses can be told apart.

Users and events are sorted by exact text, so capital letters come before lowercase. That makes no difference while user names are all lowercase, as they are in the test.
